all_videos_in_window.transcript: Here's this week's Northeast offshore fishing report breakdown. There are billfish galore in the mid-Atlantic. The white marlin open was last week and they caught almost 1,000 white marlin, blue marlin, sailfish, and spearfish. Hardly any tuna there, but the mahi fishing is also great. So, some warmer water moving to the midshore grounds, we're starting to see more yellowfin tuna mixing in with the bluefin tuna that've been around south of Long Island and off New Jersey. That fishing's picking up and we're seeing more recreational size fish moving into Cape Cod waters and perhaps even Maine. Lastly, Cheech still hasn't caught a tuna this year. For the full report, check out our YouTube channel or onthewater.com.

New Moon Cape Cod Canal Report with AJ Coots of Red Top | August Fishing Report

AJ Coots of Red Top Sporting Goods in Buzzards Bay joins Kevin Collins for a new moon canal report on August 12th. After a slow stretch, the canal is waking up — slot and above-slot fish on morning minus tides, topwater action at daybreak, bonito spotted in the canal and Cape Cod Bay, a sailfish off Chatham, and a full Buzzards Bay bottom fish update. Plus AJ breaks down exactly which plugs to pack for a squid bite vs. a mackerel bite, and a Saturday showcase on August 15th you don't want to miss.

Cape Cod Bay Bass & Bluefin with Sam Mullen of the Goose Hummock | Early August Fishing Report

Sam Mullen of the Goose Hummock in Orleans joins Kevin Collins for an early August fishing report covering Cape Cod Bay and beyond. Cape Cod Bay is still the star of the show for striped bass — and the squid bite is still ripping. Bluefish are finally filtering in. Bonito have arrived in the bay. And Sam shares the incredible story of landing a 485-pound giant bluefin on a 21-foot center console. Plus a full bottom fish update: fluke, sea bass, and the late-season sea bass extension through October 14th.

This one was sent to us by F/V Three Little Birds. Back on June 13th at Handkerchief Shoal, off Monomoy Island — a great white shark tracked, then struck a striped bass clean in half.⁠
⁠
Handkerchief Shoal is a shifting sandbar at the edge of Nantucket Sound, notorious for strong currents and shallow water that's made it treacherous for boats for centuries — but that same water has also made it one of the most productive striper and bluefish grounds on Cape Cod. Apparently the great whites know it too.⁠
⁠
Tight lines 🎣⁠
⁠
Ryan

What a week! From the surf-caught hammerhead shark in Rhode Island to the sudden push of rec-sized bluefin, a lot has happened in the last seven days! One thing that stands out, is that the fall run pregame is ramping up, we saw striped bass blitzes from Narragansett to Plymouth and the latter produced some unforgettable scenes. Bonito numbers continue to surge, especially around Cape Cod where anglers are encountering these green torpedoes from the Canal to Chatham to Wood End, and the albie clock has been set to midnight, meaning they could show at any time! There’s a whole lot more to talk about too, but you’re going to have to watch the video to get all the details.

all_videos_in_window.description:
After a brief showing in early July, the bonito are back and it seems like they’re here to stay, this time. A strong push of bones swung into the South County shoreline and moved east, with strong catches along the entire Rhody shoreline and up into Buzzards Bay. We also saw a continuation of the increasing fluke bite with good reports from Block Island, eastern Long Island Sound, Nantucket Sound and even some good reports from Duxbury Bay. Striper action continues to hold strong, but shark depredation remains a major issue throughout southern New England.

all_videos_in_window.title: August 6th, 2026 New Jersey/Delaware Bay Fishing Report with Jim Hutchinson, Jr.
all_videos_in_window.description: Some quality fluke reported out of the Shark River Inlet fleet in the past week is evidence enough of an improving bite out along the inshore sticky stuff.  We'll run down a few of the latest catches reported back to us here at The Fisherman Magazine for the New Jersey, Delaware Bay region, with fluke, sheepshead, and blowfish, perhaps backed up with a steamer-full of little necks (6:40).  Run through the August editorial lineup in the magazine, and our digital weekly (10:12) with an overview of this week's Next Cast and the connection between rays, cobia and bluefin tuna along with the latest offshore intel from Canyon Runner.  Our lead image of the week (22:10) puts a husband and wife in the right spot at the time for their wedding anniversary and a blitz of bluefish at Sandy Hook as we …

Pete Utschig of Phase Gear — the surfcaster behind Project Magic Hour and the Surfcasters documentary series — joins Peter Jenkins in Newport, mid-way through a two-week run up the coast from Florida.

raw_posts.title: Sun Aug 16 – Whale Watching
raw_posts.content: More Minke Mania and Calf Capers! Our trip today took us approximately 12 miles southeast of Montauk under clear skies and calm seas. As we approached our destination, we could see a breaching humpback from over a mile away, and knew we were in for something special. The breaching continued as we neared the young whale, a 2026 calf of a whale named Zeppelin (MTK0241), who was seen off Montauk during 2024 and was also encountered aboard yesterday’s trip. The calf alternated between breaching, flipper-slapping, lobtailing, and tail- throwing to the delight of passengers. Knowing that these behaviors are used by humpbacks to communicate with each other, and realizing that this young whale was a calf, it was no surprise when mom showed up, and the two swam side-by-side and dove in tandem. With mom likely feeding at depth, the…

raw_posts.title: Fri Aug 14 – Whale Watching
raw_posts.content: Minke (and fin whale and shark) Mania! We always begin our trips reminding passengers that we have no control over what we will see and no idea what we will encounter. That sentiment could not have been more true aboard yesterday’s trip. We first found a group of 60-80 Tamamend’s bottlenose dolphins a couple of miles from the lighthouse. After spending some time with them and a few additional pods ahead, we continued east to where we encountered humpbacks on Wednesday’s trip. Bait was sparse throughout the area, but we eventually found one finback whale, which we were able to get some good views of. A minke whale was seen in the distance and we decided to continue east looking for the humpbacks and any additional animals. Unfortunately, there were no signs of cetaceans, but there were signs of life…

raw_posts.title: Wed August 12 – Whale Watching
raw_posts.content: Humpback moms and calves in action! Under clear skies and cool ocean breezes, the Viking Starship headed east in search of the whales that have been in the region all summer, but have recently spread out as bait has also been on the move. We passed beautiful Block Island on calm seas before investigating a spout a few miles from the island. As we moved in the direction of the blow, a breach was observed to our right so we changed direction to investigate. The breaching continued as a calf rocketed to the surface numerous times in partial breaches, chin slaps, pectoral flipper slapping, and tail throws. Mom stayed alongside at the surface, before both dived down, leaving us waiting for more. After a couple of minutes, the calf surfaced, but without mom. The calf hung out at the surface…

all_videos.title: Here is your August 12th Northeast Offshore Report. Watch the full report on our channel OUT NOW.
all_videos.transcript: Here's this week's Northeast offshore fishing report breakdown. There are billfish galore in the mid-Atlantic. The white marlin open was last week and they caught almost 1,000 white marlin, blue marlin, sailfish, and spearfish. Hardly any tuna there, but the mahi fishing is also great. So, some warmer water moving to the midshore grounds, we're starting to see more yellowfin tuna mixing in with the bluefin tuna that've been around south of Long Island and off New Jersey. That fishing's picking up and we're seeing more recreational size fish moving into Cape Cod waters and perhaps even Maine. Lastly, Cheech still hasn't caught a tuna this year. For the full report, check out our YouTube channel or onthewater.com.

all_videos.description:
Cape Cod Bay Bass & Bluefin with Sam Mullen of the Goose Hummock | Early August Fishing Report

Sam Mullen of the Goose Hummock in Orleans joins Kevin Collins for an early August fishing report covering Cape Cod Bay and beyond. Cape Cod Bay is still the star of the show for striped bass — and the squid bite is still ripping. Bluefish are finally filtering in. Bonito have arrived in the bay. And Sam shares the incredible story of landing a 485-pound giant bluefin on a 21-foot center console. Plus a full bottom fish update: fluke, sea bass, and the late-season sea bass extension through October 14th.

🎣 CHAPTERS

0:00 – Intro & Welcome
0:16 – About the MFCC Podcast & Membership

all_videos.transcript: [bell] >> Welcome to the My Fishing Cape Cod podcast. The My Fishing Cape Cod podcast is your local source for the latest news and information on fishing Cape Cod. It's my pleasure now to welcome in today's featured guest and that is our good friend, Sam Mullen, of Team Goose Hummock from the Goose Hummock Shop in Orleans, Massachusetts. And Sam, welcome back to the show. How you doing this week? >> I'm doing great, Kev. It's a great to be back for another podcast. Yeah, a lot of lot of heat, lot of sun recently. But we are definitely in those dog days of summer, and it's nice to just kind of kick back and relax. And it was a great team effort. We had it We had it hanging halfway out the boat on the way back in. It was it was too big to try to get it in. And it was a little tight quarters, you know, it was hard with the with the block and tackle. But yeah, it was a great It was It was awesome. We headed out first light and we were tight by you know, probably an hour later. We don't We just got a few max and a couple squid and sent the max out and smoked the far floater and got it within an hour. It was It was a great experience. It was It was really awesome. And it was just right off the backside of Cape. So So a little farther out towards the lanes and stuff. It was pretty fun. It was a It was a good time and definitely a different you know, I've fought them in some center consoles, but nothing like you know, that small. And And it was just a very relaxed relaxed fight, which is always the best. >> And what was that fish measurement like, Sam? >> Uh it was right on 100 in. Gutted at 485. It was a solid fish. It was really nice. >> Wow, what a great experience. Now, talking a little bit more inshore, let's start off with striped bass. You and I have been going back and forth on text for most of the year. This seems to be one of the years or the summers of the boat bite. It just seems to be a little bit more productive and the quality fish a little bit more accessible by boat than they have been from shore. Um when you and I last met, Cape Cod Bay was really producing well for you and your network. Is that still the case? >> Yeah, absolutely. You know, it's been funny. You know, the bay usually this time of year is just strictly snapping wire and really just kind of just grinding it out to get at least a you know, a couple of stripers in the boat, but it is really carried on throughout into now August. Um and you know, hopefully the this month will still continue to hold some fish around in the bay. You know, it's been it's been solid with the hoochies. You know, you don't have to snap the wire or anything like that or or you know, or doll you know, just go wicked flow the tube and worm and you know, you can rip around the hoochies. The X raps are still producing. Uh even with some occasional first light topwater. Uh so, the bay has definitely been uh still a solid bite for some bass and bluefish, too. Uh starting to really filter in, but there's still some solid bass to be caught. >> And in terms of the bay and and we talk about bait so often. I know I've heard some reports of pogies up my way kind of off the coast of Plymouth, but out deeper in the middle of the bay maybe more toward like 80 to 90 ft and there's been bass and giants on those fish over the last couple of weeks. What what other baits are you hearing in different quadrants of the bay, Sam? >> Yeah, up in the way there's definitely pogies and that bias bite towards Plymouth and then towards the canals and pretty solid with some giants in there, but there you know, there's still um a a just a plethora of squid. It is 2026 is the year of the squid. It was unbelievable. But, you know, right when they showed up, it is still it's strong in number. And then now it is kind of really becoming like that again, uh from what it was years and years and years ago. Um that they become more residential into like, you know, I always call Cape Cod Bay just another great lake, you know, it's just a big pond. And sometimes they just kind of once they fall in there, they just stay around and hang out, which is the absolute best, you know, it's it's so nice and convenient. You can really kind of just pick wherever you want to go, and you especially if you go out of Suet, the Barnstable, they're centrally located. You can go up to, you know, towards Plymouth, you can go towards P-town, you can go towards, you know, Wellfleet and all that area. And and every one of those places has so productive uh because of the amount of squid. >> Now, talking about some other species, Sam, one of that I want to bring up here early in the conversation is bluefish. It's a fish that a lot of people have been looking for this season, and now that I feel like you and I are taping our first visit in the month of August, we're starting to hear some good reports of those fish in different areas. What are you hearing? >> Yeah, they are finally starting to show up. It was definitely a long time coming for these blues to come in. Um you know, but there are some that are really getting tilted into the bay, you know, uh you know, off about Barnstable, and then when you work your way east, uh there's definitely some blues, and then on the south side beaches heading towards the Monomoy, there's definitely some blues filtering in. It's always usually, especially around Monomoy and and inside, you know, uh more towards the Monomoy flats and into the Harwich area, that's last week of July right into like right now is when you get up pretty good influx, especially when you get some good southwest, and that's the case right now. I remember last year we absolutely were crushing, just uh it was best bluefish blitz I probably ever had with uh Jake, and uh it was unbelievable, and I and we're we're kind of thinking about that uh thinking about that for this year again. I'm sure that it is just going to be any one of those days where it's just going to be lights out for another like, you know, 2 to 3 weeks of just uh endless blues. >> And when you talk about bluefish, Sam, I know one of the things that frustrate a lot of anglers is when you might get into a striped bass feed, or or maybe you're kind of running and gunning for funny fish in the fall, and bluefish are kind of mixed in in different pods, and they can really chew up your gear, they can kind of snap you off. There's a lot of different frustrations with those fish, but then there's other people that really love them for the smoker, and that want to target them. But honestly, I really like just anything like 60 to 80 lb either floral or even mono is it can definitely hold up against the blues, you know, it's uh once you just know that they're that they're there and you know, you're not going to be catching any bass, just have some really heavy uh leader line on board at this time of year to be able to just tie on a new leader. So, then you you stop losing so many plugs and and then you you'll you know, you use the definitely like the tactical angle clip that you kind of not direct connection to any kind of line, so they won't be chasing that you know, chafing off at all. And uh you know, and then obviously, you know, a single hooks are always kind of nice if you want to just not get too crazy with them and hook them all the time into their head and be careful with them they're thrashing and obviously those teeth can definitely take off some digits if uh you don't want to lose any fingers. >> And another species I want to ask now that we're in the fall is uh bonito. I started to hear their presence be made known last weekend out at Monomoy, but I'm sure if that was kind of really the first action they've kind of matriculated and filtered into other areas as well. >> Yeah, definitely. I've heard them into Monomoy and uh you know, yeah, like it is that time of end of July, beginning of August, those you know, everybody starts to get that itch of those funny fish and those and those bonito are filtering in. And even better, those bonito have been popping around up in the bay as of the past couple days, which is wicked exciting. And the best thing about the bonito is they're definitely less finicky than the albies. And they will just hit I mean, they hit topwater poppers. And you know, even if they're in shallower water, um you know, they are quick. You know, they still have to go chase them a little bit and everything, but man, when you can get on a feed like that, you can definitely capitalize and uh definitely have a lot of fun catching those bonito. >> And any rough idea, Sam? Obviously not looking to burn spots of where these fish are in Cape Cod Bay, cuz this is the first report I'm hearing of them in the bay. >> Yeah, it's definitely been like more towards uh you know, uh Billingsgate and north. Um they've definitely been scattered. Um and it is a you know, just the very beginning, you know, there's just been some murmurs, but nothing really uh super concentrated. You know, but just definitely like the the general area of uh Billingsgate is uh from what I've been hearing. >> Last but not least, I always like to check in on the bottom fish with you, and it's been a really good productive year, it seems, in a variety of areas for fluke. I've heard of them being successfully targeted even from shore in the Buzzards Bay area, which is really really cool and a great opportunity, but also the boat guys seem to really be having a lot of success with those guys, and I'm hearing a late summer push of sea bass as well. A lot of anglers looking for fluke and coming up with really nice sea bass. >> Yeah, absolutely. Yeah, around Monomoy and even north of Monomoy and uh that area has been great uh for fluke and uh and there's definitely been some big sea bass in the mix. And yeah, even guys that have been I don't know, commercial bass and at night have uh been catching big fluke, which is pretty cool. Which actually, commercial bass, as on a side note, did close, and they reached their quota. But uh to get back on to topic, uh yeah, the fluke has been great, and uh this is like when you can really enjoy the ground fishing. Uh I feel like with the fluke, if you go to Monomoy, you can really just kind of hop around from shoal to shoal and and really be able to get on some good fluke, especially if you start to creep a little uh southeasterly. And and you know, you don't have to go to Nantucket, but if you really kind of just work about 8 to 10 mi uh south south to southeast of Monomoy, you can really get some good fluke this time of year. And also bycatch, you know, if you get into some really deeper water, you can get into some good sea bass. >> And speaking of sea bass, I think it's just important to remind folks that that season has been extended all the way through October 14th. You can still have a two fish per person limit per angler, and the the minimum size still 16 in, so just another great extended opportunity now in the fall to get some of that delicious sea bass meat for the freezer in the winter. >> Absolutely. I mean, especially with the warmer water warmer water temps that we've been experiencing the past couple falls, you can definitely still get some pretty pretty darn good sea bass fishing all the way through October. Tight lines. >> My thanks to Sam Mullen of the Goose Hummock Shop and Team Goose Hummock for joining us on this edition of the My Fishing Cape Cod Podcast. all_videos.title: Great White Shark Bites Striped Bass in Half
all_videos.description:
This one was sent to us by F/V Three Little Birds. Back on June 13th at Handkerchief Shoal, off Monomoy Island — a great white shark tracked, then struck a striped bass clean in half.⁠
⁠
Handkerchief Shoal is a shifting sandbar at the edge of Nantucket Sound, notorious for strong currents and shallow water that's made it treacherous for boats for centuries — but that same water has also made it one of the most productive striper and bluefish grounds on Cape Cod. Apparently the great whites know it too.⁠
⁠
Tight lines 🎣⁠
⁠

all_videos.description:
What a week! From the surf-caught hammerhead shark in Rhode Island to the sudden push of rec-sized bluefin, a lot has happened in the last seven days! One thing that stands out, is that the fall run pregame is ramping up, we saw striped bass blitzes from Narragansett to Plymouth and the latter produced some unforgettable scenes. Bonito numbers continue to surge, especially around Cape Cod where anglers are encountering these green torpedoes from the Canal to Chatham to Wood End, and the albie clock has been set to midnight, meaning they could show at any time! There’s a whole lot more to talk about too, but you’re going to have to watch the video to get all the details.

all_videos.description: This week's Long Island Video Fishing Forecast comes from Island Yacht's new marina in Bay Shore, where we take a tour of the facility with Chet before diving into another action-packed fishing report. We preview new Daiwa and Tsunami gear from ICAST, plug Episode 20 of The Fisherman Podcast—covering the booming shark bite, nearshore bluefin tuna, triggerfish tactics, and menhaden management—and bring you the latest Canyon Runner offshore update. Around the Island, anglers are enjoying steady fluke action, quality bluefin tuna, bull sharks, sheepshead, striped bass, Spanish mackerel, mahi, and more, highlighted by great catches from both boats and the surf. Seven species, 70 leaderboard spots, and one Steiger Craft grand prize—the 2026 Dream Boat Fishing Challenge gets underway May 1st.

Every fishing season has its moments. The first spring blackfish that thumps a jig in chilly April water. A fluke drifting across a sandy edge in July. The unmistakable run of a big bluefish cutting through a late-summer tide. Those moments are what keep anglers coming back to the water year after year. For many fishermen, those experiences are reward enough. But for a dedicated group of anglers across the Northeast, the season carries an added element of competition.

all_videos.title: August 6th 2026 New England Video Fishing Forecast with Dave Anderson
all_videos.description:
After a brief showing in early July, the bonito are back and it seems like they’re here to stay, this time. A strong push of bones swung into the South County shoreline and moved east, with strong catches along the entire Rhody shoreline and up into Buzzards Bay. We also saw a continuation of the increasing fluke bite with good reports from Block Island, eastern Long Island Sound, Nantucket Sound and even some good reports from Duxbury Bay. Striper action continues to hold strong, but shark depredation remains a major issue throughout southern New England.

all_videos.title: August 6th, 2026 New Jersey/Delaware Bay Fishing Report with Jim Hutchinson, Jr.
all_videos.description: Some quality fluke reported out of the Shark River Inlet fleet in the past week is evidence enough of an improving bite out along the inshore sticky stuff.  We'll run down a few of the latest catches reported back to us here at The Fisherman Magazine for the New Jersey, Delaware Bay region, with fluke, sheepshead, and blowfish, perhaps backed up with a steamer-full of little necks (6:40).  Run through the August editorial lineup in the magazine, and our digital weekly (10:12) with an overview of this week's Next Cast and the connection between rays, cobia and bluefin tuna along with the latest offshore intel from Canyon Runner.  Our lead image of the week (22:10) puts a husband and wife in the right spot at the time for their wedding anniversary and a blitz of bluefish at Sandy Hook as we …

all_videos.description: This week's Long Island Video Fishing Forecast comes from Island Yacht's new marina in Bay Shore, where we take a tour of the facility with Chet before diving into another action-packed fishing report. We preview new Daiwa and Tsunami gear from ICAST, plug Episode 20 of The Fisherman Podcast—covering the booming shark bite, nearshore bluefin tuna, triggerfish tactics, and menhaden management—and bring you the latest Canyon Runner offshore update. Around the Island, anglers are enjoying steady fluke action, quality bluefin tuna, bull sharks, sheepshead, striped bass, Spanish mackerel, mahi, and more, highlighted by great catches from both boats and the surf. We also feature Dream Boat Challenge updates, magazine previews, a new correspondent segment with Mark Sedotti on crushing barbs for s…

all_videos.title: "The Best Time to Fish Is Anytime You Can" — Pete Utschig on fishing travel - Saltwater Edge Podcast
all_videos.description:
Pete Utschig of Phase Gear — the surfcaster behind Project Magic Hour and the Surfcasters documentary series — joins Peter Jenkins in Newport, mid-way through a two-week run up the coast from Florida.

Pete explains how a single weekend trip 15 years ago turned Florida's beaches into his home water, how an Airbnb guide service grew into a full all-inclusive surf fishing lodge (December–April, rods, lures, and food included — bring board shorts), and why his bucket list is made of fish, not places: cubera snapper, giant trevally in Indonesia, corvina in Ecuador, giant tarpon in Gabon, and bluefin tuna from the rocks in Europe. Plus the philosophy that holds it all together: you can't control the tides, but you can control the vibes — and the best time to fish is anytime you can.
